expectations.text: There is exactly one implementation-neutral source of truth for the model (no database-specific types in it), and the PostgreSQL DDL and JSON Schema are generated from it rather than written by hand in parallel
expectations.evidence: datamodel/model.yaml is the canonical model with neutral types only (uuid, geometry, decimal, date, enumerations). exports/draft/schema.sql header: 'Generated by dmtool from UrbanTreeCadastre 0.1.0 ... Do not edit; regenerate.' Grader re-ran dmtool export (postgres, jsonschema) on model.yaml: output is byte-identical to exports/draft/schema.sql and schema.json. Hand-written parts (exchange envelope, tuning.sql) reference the generated output rather than redefining structures (D-009, D-013).

expectations.text: Assumptions and/or open questions are written to a file in datamodel/
expectations.evidence: datamodel/open-questions.md lists Q-001..Q-011 and A-001..A-016, each 'confirmed: no'; decisions.md marks all 14 decisions 'without user confirmation'.

expectations.text: Species is modelled as a managed, extensible code list or reference table rather than free text
expectations.evidence: model.yaml class Species (id, botanicalName unique, commonName, gbifTaxonKey, active); association TreeSpecies to Species multiplicity 1; generated DDL has species table with FK. D-004 explains why it is a class (~900 entries, extended by arborists).

expectations.text: Inspection records are protected from deletion and have an audit trail (who changed what, when)
expectations.evidence: Inspection has history {mode: audit, deletion: logical}; generated schema.sql creates inspection_history; tuning.sql: 'CREATE TRIGGER inspection_no_delete BEFORE DELETE ON inspection ... forbid_delete()' and a write_history() trigger recording operation, recorded_by (app.user/current_user) and row_data for inspection and other entity tables. Defect child rows are not history-triggered; this is acknowledged in a NOTE.

expectations.text: Corrections of a tree's location are historised so the previous location and the correction time can be retrieved
expectations.evidence: Class TreeLocationCorrection (correctedAt, previousLocation Point EPSG:25832, reason, correctedBy) as composition of Tree; generated table tree_location_correction with previous_location geometry(Point,25832) and corrected_at. D-008. Note: no trigger fills it automatically on UPDATE of tree.location (relies on the application), but the structure supports retrieval.

expectations.text: Felled trees are kept with felling date and reason, and a felled tree can be linked to one or more replacement trees
expectations.evidence: Tree.status (standing/felled), fellingDate, fellingReason (extensible FellingReason list); association TreeReplacement replacementTrees 0..* / replacedTree 0..1, generated as tree.replaced_tree_id FK. C-001 CHECK in tuning.sql ties felling fields to status. Example file shows a felled tree with a replacement.

expectations.text: The tree location is a PostGIS Point geometry with SRID 25832 and has a spatial (GiST) index, in the generated DDL or in a separate tuning script
expectations.evidence: Generated schema.sql: 'location geometry(Point,25832) NOT NULL'; tuning.sql: 'CREATE INDEX tree_location_gix ON tree USING gist (location) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;'.

expectations.text: Defects are modelled as multi-valued entries each with a severity (low/medium/high), not as comma-separated text
expectations.evidence: Class InspectionDefect (defectType, severity: DefectSeverity low/medium/high) composed 0..* in Inspection; generated table inspection_defect with severity defect_severity ENUM('low','medium','high') NOT NULL and FK to the defect_type lookup.

expectations.text: Expected volumes (trees, inspections per year, measures per year) are recorded per object type in the model, not only in prose
expectations.evidence: model.yaml nfr per class: Tree 'volume: 180000, growth: 3000/year'; Inspection 'growth: 200000/year', retention 30 years; Measure 'growth: 25000/year'; also Species 900, Site 5000, StaffMember 50.

expectations.text: Inspector names are flagged as personal data and excluded from the open data export
expectations.evidence: StaffMember nfr classification: personal; name description 'Full name. Personal data - must not appear in open data or the exchange file.' tuning.sql open_data_tree view selects only id, tree_number, botanical_name, gbif_taxon_key, planting_year, location and latest vitality, with no staff reference.

expectations.text: The exchange file for the regional agency carries no inspector names (at most an internal or pseudonymous id)
expectations.evidence: Exchange envelope has no staff array (D-009/D-011); Inspection in generated schema.json has only 'inspector' as a UUID reference; the schema is closed. Grader test: adding inspectorName to an inspection is rejected.

expectations.text: The generated JSON Schema is a valid JSON Schema, and a realistic example exchange file validates against it
expectations.evidence: Grader validated schema.json and exchange-file.schema.json with Draft202012Validator.check_schema (OK) and validated handwritten/example-exchange-file.json against the envelope (with local GeoJSON Point/Geometry stubs for the remote $refs): 0 errors. Bad severity and malformed point are rejected. Example is realistic (UTM32 coordinates, felled tree with replacement, defects, done measure).

expectations.text: Each model element can be traced to its source (source IDs on the elements or a traceability table to requirements.md / legacy_trees.sql)
expectations.evidence: Elements carry 'sources: [S1, S2]' etc. and decision refs; sources.md defines S1=requirements.md, S2=legacy_trees.sql, S3=GBIF, S4=Roloff; handwritten/legacy-mapping.md maps legacy columns. Some attributes/constraints lack their own sources but inherit class-level sources.

expectations.text: For tree species, the run checks for a standardised taxonomy or vocabulary (e.g. GBIF Backbone Taxonomy, World Flora Online) and either recommends reusing it, with a verifiable source and a fit assessment, or explains why the city's own species list is kept; it does not adopt a vocabulary silently
expectations.evidence: sources.md S3: GBIF Backbone Taxonomy, 'Tilia cordata -> taxon key 3152047, verified', URL https://api.gbif.org/v1/species/match, retrieved 2026-11-23; candidate table verdict: 'Keep the city's own list (cultivars...) but link each entry via optional gbifTaxonKey - D-004. Not adopted until you confirm.' D-004 gives the fit assessment; WFO named as an unchecked alternative. Field is marked status: proposed.

claims.claim: The model passes the steward tool's validation with no errors
claims.evidence: Grader ran dmtool validate: '0 error(s), 1 warning(s)' (proposed elements).

claims.claim: An extra field such as an inspector name is rejected
The SQL has not been run against a database

claims.evidence: Changing a standing tree to status 'felled' without fellingDate still validates against the exchange schema (C-001 is only in SQL).

suggestions.assertion: Assumptions and/or open questions are written to a file in datamodel/
suggestions.reason: Non-discriminating: both runs pass trivially; the prompt explicitly asks for written assumptions. Consider checking that specific conflicts (Roloff 1-5 vs 0-3, legacy felled trees without date) are raised as questions.

suggestions.assertion: Inspector names are flagged as personal data and excluded from the open data export
suggestions.reason: Non-discriminating: both runs pass. Could be tightened, e.g. require that the open data export also excludes inspector pseudonyms and audit users.

suggestions.assertion: Corrections of a tree's location are historised so the previous location and the correction time can be retrieved
suggestions.reason: Passes on structure alone; it does not check that a correction is captured automatically (without_skill has a trigger on UPDATE OF location, with_skill relies on the application). Consider requiring a mechanism that guarantees capture.

No assertion checks that the exchange JSON Schema enforces business rules (e.g. a felled tree requires fellingDate/reason). with_skill's schema accepts status 'felled' without a date; without_skill's rejects it.
No assertion covers the legacy migration (without_skill wrote a full migration script; with_skill only a mapping doc) or offline client-generated IDs; both handled IDs, but migration depth differs.

eval_feedback.overall: Most assertions are achievable by any competent run; the discriminating ones are #1 (single source), #9 (volumes in model) and #14 (vocabulary), which partly encode the skill's own method.
